searchText: Hey <@552133098075193354> , what do you think are the chances that 1559 is not ready by the time the London HF needs to rollout? <10%? It could happen, but I think it's extremely unlikely I think the way to make sure it happens is to not add anything else to London until 1559 is ready thanks Tim btw was curious to know what the plan would be if it does not get implemented? I asked Micah this before and he wasn’t sure about it just want to make sure we have consensus between Geth and Besu before sharing those tests. Because we are currently working on transaction encoding / decoding once we have consensus between Geth and Besu <@!524738020033691659> will be able to provide tests for tx hashes and signatures Great - I will wait for these test to ensure we are correct as well 🙂 Is there any plan for EIPs that defines how new transactions will be sent by RPC? I know that we have sendRawTransaction. However, are we planning to modify sendTransaction also? What is the correct RLP for the new transaction type? I see that the client implementations have a different order than documentation. Documentation transaction payload RLP is: rlp([chainId, nonce, maxInclusionFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, access_list, signatureYParity, signatureR, signatureS]). What is in the client implementations is: [nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, maxInclusionFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, signatureYParity, signatureR, signatureS]. Which client implementation are you looking at? https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum-EIP1559/blob/master/core/types/transaction.go#L162 https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/blob/master/ethereum/core/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/core/encoding/TransactionDecoder.java#L174 The go implementation is obsolete Go implementation is: https://github.com/quilt/go-ethereum/tree/eip1559 Latest Besu version: https://github.com/abdelhamidbakhta/besu/tree/playground <@!574864862338088960> thx, now it's clear for me Well, it depends: if it's a slight delay, then the difficulty bomb will go off and we'll deploy shortly after, which is not great. If it's a massive delay we could split London and remove the difficulty bomb, but that's very unlikely. thanks for the reply! makes sense now
